summary: The note explains how to generate a playing-card deck (52 cards) that is asynchronous and deterministic, so a user can reveal cards one at a time without exposing the whole deck. It uses a seed passed from the frontend with a position number, and PHP's mt_srand/mt_rand with array_multisort to produce a consistent shuffle. It closes by suggesting improvements such as hiding the seed by modifying it or storing seeds in a database so only the backend controls them.
one_line: A method for generating a reproducible, card-by-card shuffled 52-card deck using seeded random numbers, with ways to hide the seed.
key_facts: There are 52! unique ways of shuffling a standard 52-card deck, roughly 8e68.
The author's project required that each card be returned only when the user wants to reveal it, not the whole deck at once.
The system must be asynchronous, so a user requests a single card at a time rather than the whole deck.
The system must be deterministic, so querying a second card should draw from the same deck as the first.
Calling srand(42) in PHP produces the same sequence of random numbers on each page load, though results may depend on the environment.
The example sets the seed with mt_srand($seed) in the showCards function.
The deck list CARDS_LIST uses codes S1-S13, H1-H13, D1-D13 and C1-C13 for spades, hearts, diamonds and clubs.
The showCards function shuffles by generating mt_rand() values for each card and calling array_multisort($order, $cards).
showCards returns $cards[$position - 1], so the frontend supplies a position from 1 to 52.
The author states the approach gives a fully functional system that draws any card from any position without exposing other cards.
A suggested improvement is to hide the seed by modifying it with an algorithm, for example multiplying it by 2.
A second suggested improvement is to store seeds in a database and return only an ID to the frontend, so the backend controls the seed.
The author says the principles can be adapted to other decks, such as Magic: The Gathering cards.
The author writes the example code in PHP and Angular and says the concepts apply to any programming language.
The author is a software engineer at Amazon who writes about programming, UX and interviewing.
